column1: Hormone levels – and hence our moods – may be affected by the weather.
column2: 激素水平——因而我们的情绪——可能受天气影响。

column1: Gloomy weather can cause depression, but sunshine appears to raise the spirits.
column2: 阴沉的天气容易让人感到沮丧，而阳光则似乎能够提升人的情绪。

column1: In Britain, for example, the dull weather of winter drastically cuts down the amount of sunlight that is experienced which strongly affects some people.
column2: 例如，在英国，冬季的阴沉天气会大大减少人们接触阳光的时间，这会对一些人产生严重影响。

column1: They become so depressed and lacking in energy that their work and social life are affected.
column2: 他们变得沮丧且缺乏精力，工作和社交生活都受到影响。

column1: This condition has been given the name SAD (Seasonal Affective Disorder).
column2: 这种病症被命名为‘季节性情感障碍’。

column1: Sufferers can fight back by making the most of any sunlight in winter and by spending a few hours each day under special, full-spectrum lamps.
column2: 患者可以通过利用冬季的阳光来对抗这种状况，同时每天在特殊的全光谱灯下度过几个小时也会有所帮助。

column1: These provide more ultraviolet and blue-green light than ordinary fluorescent and tungsten lights.
column2: 这些光源比普通的荧光灯和钨丝灯能发出更多的紫外线和蓝绿色光。

column1: Some Russian scientists claim that children learn better after being exposed to ultraviolet light.
column2: 一些俄罗斯科学家声称，儿童在接触紫外线后学习效果会更好。

column1: In warm countries, hours of work are often arranged so that workers can take a break, or even a siesta, during the hottest part of the day.
column2: 在温暖的国家里，工作时间通常会被安排得如此合理，以至于工人们在一天中最热的时候可以休息一会儿，甚至小睡一觉。

column1: Scientists are working to discover the links between the weather and human beings’ moods and performance.
column2: 科学家们正在努力探索天气与人类情绪和表现之间的关系。

column1: It is generally believed that tempers grow shorter in hot, muggy weather.
column2: 人们普遍认为，在炎热潮湿的天气里，人的脾气会变得更易急躁。

column1: There is no doubt that ‘crimes against the person’ rise in the summer, when the weather is hotter and fall in the winter when the weather is colder.
column2: 毫无疑问，在夏季天气炎热时，针对个人的犯罪会增加；而在冬季天气寒冷时，此类犯罪则会减少。

column1: Research in the United States has shown a relationship between temperature and street riots.
column2: 美国的研究表明，温度与街头骚乱之间存在关联。

column1: The frequency of riots rises dramatically as the weather gets warmer, hitting a peak around 27-30°C.
column2: 随着天气变暖，骚乱的频率显著上升，在气温达到27至30摄氏度时达到峰值。

column1: But is this effect really due to a mood change caused by the heat?
column2: 但这种效果是否真的源于高温引起的情绪变化？

column1: Some scientists argue that trouble starts more often in hot weather merely because there are more people in the street when the weather is good.
column2: 一些科学家认为，问题在炎热天气下更频繁出现，仅仅是因为好天气时街上的人更多。

column1: Psychologists have also studied how being cold affects performance.
column2: 心理学家也研究了寒冷对表现的影响。

column1: Researchers compared divers working in icy cold water at 5°C with others in water at 20°C (about swimming pool temperature).
column2: 研究人员将在5摄氏度冰寒水中工作的人与在20摄氏度（约泳池温度）水中工作的人进行了比较。

column1: The colder water made the divers worse at simple arithmetic and other mental tasks.
column2: 较冷的水使潜水员在简单算术和其他心智任务上的表现变差。

column1: But significantly, their performance was impaired as soon as they were put into the cold water – before their bodies had time to cool down.
column2: 但值得注意的是，一旦进入冷水，其表现便立即下降——甚至在身体有时间冷却之前就已经如此。

column1: This suggests that the low temperature did not slow down mental functioning directly, but the feeling of cold distracted the divers from their tasks.
column2: 这表明，低温并未直接减缓大脑功能，而是寒冷的感觉让潜水员分心，无法集中注意力完成任务。

column1: Psychologists have conducted studies showing that people become less sceptical and more optimistic when the weather is sunny However, this apparently does not just depend on the temperature.
column2: 心理学家的研究表明，当天气晴朗时，人们会变得不那么怀疑、更加乐观，但这种现象显然并不只取决于温度。

column1: An American psychologist studied customers in a temperature-controlled restaurant.
column2: 一位美国心理学家对一家温控餐厅的顾客进行了研究。

column1: They gave bigger tips when the sun was shining and smaller tips when it wasn’t, even though the temperature in the restaurant was the same.
column2: 当阳光明媚时，他们给出的小费会更多；而天气不好时，小费则会减少，尽管餐厅内的温度其实是相同的。

column1: A link between weather and mood is made believable by the evidence for a connection between behaviour and the length of the daylight hours.
column2: 天气与情绪之间的联系因行为与日照时长之间存在关联而变得可信。

column1: This, in turn, might involve the level of a hormone called melatonin, produced in the pineal gland in the brain.
column2: 这可能涉及大脑松果体产生的激素褪黑素的水平。

column1: The amount of melatonin falls with greater exposure to daylight.
column2: 褪黑素水平随日光暴露增加而下降。

column1: Research shows that melatonin plays an important part in the seasonal behaviour of certain animals.
column2: 研究表明，褪黑素在某些动物的季节性行为中起着重要作用。

column1: For example, food consumption of stags increases during the winter, reaching a peak in February/ March.
column2: 例如，雄鹿的食物摄入量在冬季会增加，并在二月或三月达到高峰。

column1: It falls again to a low point in May, then rises to a peak in September, before dropping to another minimum in November.
column2: 这一数值在五月再次降至最低点，然后在九月达到峰值，之后又在十一月降至新的最低点。

column1: These changes seem to be triggered by varying melatonin levels.
column2: 这些变化似乎是由褪黑素水平的差异所引发的。

column1: In the laboratory, hamsters put on more weight when the nights are getting shorter and their melatonin levels are falling.
column2: 在实验室中，当夜晚变短、褪黑激素水平下降时，仓鼠的体重也会增加。

column1: On the other hand, if they are given injections of melatonin, they will stop eating altogether.
column2: 另一方面，如果它们被注射了褪黑激素，那么它们就会完全停止进食。
column3: On the other hand|另一方面

column1: It seems that time cues provided by the changing lengths of day and night trigger changes in animals’ behaviour – changes that are needed to cope with the cycle of the seasons.
column2: 看来，由昼夜长短变化所引发的时间信号，会促使动物的行为发生改变——这些改变正是为了适应季节更替而必需的。

column1: People’s moods too, have been shown to react to the length of the daylight hours.
column2: 人们的心情也受到白天时长的影响。

column1: Sceptics might say that longer exposure to sunshine puts people in a better mood because they associate it with the happy feelings of holidays and freedom from responsibility.
column2: 怀疑论者可能会认为，长时间暴露在阳光下会让人心情更好，因为他们将阳光与假期中的愉悦感以及摆脱责任的感觉联系在一起。

column1: However, the belief that rain and murky weather make people more unhappy is borne out by a study in Belgium, which showed that a telephone counselling service gets more telephone calls from people with suicidal feelings when it rains.
column2: 然而，比利时的一项研究证实了‘下雨或天气阴沉会让人更不快乐’这一观点。该研究显示，下雨时，有自杀念头的人更倾向于拨打心理咨询服务电话。

column1: When there is a thunderstorm brewing, some people complain of the air being ‘heavy’ and of feeling irritable, moody and on edge.
column2: 当暴风雨即将来临之际，有些人会抱怨空气变得‘沉重’，同时感到烦躁、情绪不稳定，容易紧张不安。

column1: They may be reacting to the fact that the air can become slightly positively charged when large thunderclouds are generating the intense electrical fields that cause lightning flashes.
column2: 他们可能是因为当巨大的雷云产生强烈电场时，空气会略微带上正电荷，而这种正电荷正是引发闪电的原因。

column1: The positive charge increases the levels of serotonin (a chemical involved in sending signals in the nervous system).
column2: 正电荷会提高血清素的水平，而血清素是一种参与神经系统信号传递的化学物质。

column1: High levels of serotonin in certain areas of the nervous system make people more active and reactive and, possibly, more aggressive.
column2: 神经系统某些区域血清素水平较高，会使人变得更加活跃、反应更敏捷，甚至可能变得更具攻击性。

column1: When certain winds are blowing, such as the Mistral in southern France and the Fohn in southern Germany, mood can be affected – and the number of traffic accidents rises.
column2: 当某些特定风向吹拂时，比如法国南部的马斯特拉风以及德国南部的福恩风，就会影响人们的情绪，进而增加交通事故的发生几率。

column1: It may be significant that the concentration of positively charged particles is greater than normal in these winds.
column2: 值得注意的是，这些风中正电荷粒子的浓度高于正常水平。

column1: In the United Kingdom, 400,000 ionizers are sold every year.
column2: 在英国，每年有40万台离子发生器被售出。

column1: These small machines raise the number of negative ions in the air in a room.
column2: 这些小型机器能够增加房间内的负离子数量。

column1: Many people claim they feel better in negatively charged air.
column2: 许多人声称在负电空气环境中感觉更好。
